Co-Selling With Platforms

The Commercial SystemPart 18

By lowob · 17 September 2026 · Updated 16 November 2026 · 9-minute read · Distribution

Co-selling is a structured arrangement in which a vendor and a platform's sales team work the same customer opportunity: the vendor shares deals with the platform, the platform's account team supports them, and, once the vendor has earned it, the platform refers opportunities back. The large cloud programmes, including AWS's ACE programme and Microsoft's partner programme, provide the mechanics. Whether they produce anything depends on one question: does your product grow the platform's own number? Platform sellers are measured on their platform's revenue, consumption and customer outcomes, and they spend time on partners that move those. A vendor that cannot show how it does will share pipeline and receive little back.

The usual experience runs like this. A vendor joins a cloud partner programme, lists on the marketplace, and shares a handful of opportunities through the partner portal. Months pass. The platform's account managers do not call. The partner manager concludes co-selling does not work.

It can work, but the arrangement has a logic that many vendors miss. Part 14 of this series covers partner channels where the vendor recruits partners to sell its product. Co-selling reverses the direction: the vendor is the partner, and the platform decides whether to spend its sellers' time on it. Part 16 covers marketplace listings, the transaction route that co-selling often depends on.

What platform sellers want

A platform's account manager has a target, a set of accounts and too many partners asking for attention. The partners who get time are those who help the account manager hit the target. The design of the partner programmes makes that explicit.

Programme featureWhat it rewardsSource
AWS services tiers: Select, Advanced, PremierCertified people, and launched customer opportunities with minimum monthly revenue (3 opportunities at Select, 20 at Advanced, 50 at Premier)AWS Services Partner Tiers
AWS ACE programmeSharing and updating opportunities; discounts for originating new customer opportunities; eligibility to receive AWS referralsAWS ACE programme page
Microsoft partner capability scoreNet customer adds, certifications, customers' usage growth and deployments; 70 of 100 points to qualify for a designationMicrosoft Learn
Microsoft Partner Admin LinkAutomatic attribution of influenced and Azure-consumed revenue to the partner's access in the customer's environmentMicrosoft Learn
Microsoft Azure IP co-sell eligible statusAt least $100,000 of Azure consumed revenue over a trailing 12 months, or $100,000 of cumulative marketplace billed revenue; a transactable offer primarily platformed on AzureMicrosoft Learn
Google Cloud Partner Network tiers and competenciesTiers (Select, Premier, Diamond) based on joint customer outcomes; competencies measured on certifications and contributions to validated closed/won opportunitiesGoogle Cloud

Every row measures customer outcomes on the platform: launched workloads, usage growth, deployments, consumed or marketplace-billed revenue, closed opportunities. None measures the vendor's revenue outside the platform. A vendor whose product increases the customer's cloud consumption, or speeds up a migration, or brings a new workload onto the platform, has something to offer the account manager. A vendor whose product runs anywhere and consumes little has a weaker case, however good the product.

The scale explains why platforms invest in this. Canalys forecast that 70% of customer spending on technology, IT services and telecom services would go through partners in 2025. Platforms rely on partners to reach and serve customers, and their programmes are built to direct partner effort toward the platform's growth.

How the mechanics work

The programmes differ in detail but share a structure: register, share pipeline, attribute influence, and transact.

StepOn AWSOn MicrosoftWhat the vendor should do
JoinJoin the partner network at no cost and accept the ACE terms in Partner CentralJoin the AI Cloud Partner Program; reach co-sell-ready status with a published marketplace offer, a complete business profile, a sales contact per co-sell geography, a one-pager and a pitch deckChoose one platform first, based on where most of your customers run
Share pipelineSubmit opportunities to the ACE Pipeline Manager and keep them updated through the opportunity's lifeCo-sell opportunities in Partner Center, shared with Microsoft sales teams or other partners, or logged as private deals for Microsoft's reportingShare only qualified opportunities, with accurate stage and value
Attribute influenceLaunched opportunities count toward tier requirementsPartner Admin Link and Digital Partner of Record link the partner to customer subscriptionsSet up attribution with every customer, or the influence will not be credited
TransactMarketplace private offers; some purchases count toward customer spend commitmentsMicrosoft Marketplace; sales of Azure IP co-sell eligible offers count toward customers' Azure consumption commitments (MACC)Route suitable deals through the marketplace (Part 16)
ReceiveBecome ACE-eligible to receive AWS referralsMicrosoft sales teams can identify and share opportunities with co-sell partnersRespond fast; a slow reply to a platform referral is rarely forgiven

Two details are easy to miss. On Microsoft, Digital Partner of Record can be set only by the customer, one partner per subscription, while Partner Admin Link requires the partner's user or service principal to have access in the customer's environment. If the vendor does not set these up, its influence on the customer's consumption may never be credited. On AWS, funding programmes such as marketing development funds are available only from the Advanced tier, and partner opportunity acceleration funding for proofs of concept from Select, so tier progress affects what support a vendor can request.

Google Cloud is changing its structure. It announced the Google Cloud Partner Network in December 2025 for rollout in the first quarter of 2026, applying to ISVs and services partners alike. Tiers are based on customer outcomes, and engagements are applied automatically toward a partner's tier and competency progress. Its announcement says the programme rewards successful co-sell efforts but does not set out the co-sell mechanics.

These descriptions come from each platform's own documentation and change regularly. Check the current terms before building a plan around any benefit.

What co-selling costs

Co-selling looks free because joining is free. The real costs are people, time, data and dependence.

Certified people. AWS's services tiers require accredited and certified individuals, from four accredited individuals and four certifications at Select to twenty accredited individuals and thirty-five certifications at Premier. Microsoft's capability score includes skilling metrics. For a 50- to 500-person firm, certifying staff is a real cost in time.

A partner manager's time. Opportunities must be kept updated through their life. A pipeline shared once and left stale signals a partner not worth the account manager's time.

Pipeline data. Sharing an opportunity means telling the platform the customer, the deal size and the stage. Check what your customer contracts allow, agree internally what is shared and what is not, and record the rule. Some customers will not want a platform told about a purchase before it is signed.

Dependence. A vendor whose pipeline comes mainly from one platform's referrals has moved its single-channel risk rather than removed it. Our piece Single-channel dependency covers the warning signs.

Platform sellers are paid on the platform's number. Show how you grow it, or expect silence.

Four stages, in order

Most vendors move through co-selling in four stages. Each needs the one before it, and trying to skip ahead is the most common reason the arrangement stalls.

StageWhat happensEvidence the vendor needsSignal to move on
1. ListedMarketplace listing live; partner programme joinedA product that runs on the platform and a clear description of the workload it bringsFirst deals transacted through the marketplace
2. SharingVendor shares qualified opportunities and keeps them updatedAccurate pipeline; attribution set up with customersPlatform account managers start responding on shared deals
3. ReceivingPlatform sellers refer opportunities to the vendorLaunched customers, tier requirements met, a short case for how the product grows consumptionReferrals arrive without being chased
4. Joint planningVendor and platform agree target accounts and plans togetherA record of co-sold wins and their effect on platform consumptionNamed contacts on both sides and a shared account list

The evidence at stage 3 is a single page an account manager can use: which workloads the product brings to the platform, what consumption a typical customer adds, and two or three customers willing to be named. That page is often what changes the relationship.

Measuring whether co-selling pays

Four numbers, tracked quarterly, tell a vendor whether the arrangement earns its cost.

MeasureQuestion
Co-sold win rate against non-co-soldDo deals with platform involvement win more often?
Cycle time, co-sold against notDoes platform involvement shorten the deal?
Platform-referred pipelineIs the platform sending deals, or only receiving them?
Stakeholders added per co-sold dealDid the platform's account team open doors the vendor could not?

The last is worth tracking because breadth of contact predicts outcomes. Ebsta's 2024 benchmarks, drawn from 4.2 million opportunities, found won deals had about nine engaged contacts at the solution stage against about two in lost deals. A platform account team that knows the customer's architecture and budget holders can add contacts a vendor would take months to reach. The Ebsta figure is correlational; it does not prove the platform caused the win.

Co-selling decisions, such as which platform to commit to, which certifications to fund and what pipeline data to share, belong in the decision record The Build Order describes (The commercial decisions worth recording). The data-sharing rule in particular is a decision someone will later need to defend, and our piece Nothing sends without a person applies: no opportunity should be shared with a platform automatically without a named person approving what goes.

Illustrative example: an observability vendor moves from sharing to receiving
Decision
Commit to one cloud platform for co-selling, fund the certifications for its next tier, and write a one-page case for platform account managers.
Reason and owner
A year of sharing opportunities had produced no referrals; most customers ran on that platform and the product typically increased their monitored workloads. Owned by the head of partnerships, with sales leadership agreeing the data-sharing rule.
What changed
Attribution was set up with every live customer, shared opportunities were updated weekly, and co-sold win rate and cycle time were reported quarterly beside non-co-sold deals.

Illustrative: a composite of a mid-size observability software vendor, built from patterns across engagements.

lowob takeaways

  • Show how you grow the platform's number. Platform programmes reward customer consumption and outcomes, not your revenue.
  • Set up attribution with every customer. On Microsoft, influence that is not linked may never be credited.
  • Count the real costs. Certified staff, a partner manager's time, pipeline data and the risk of dependence.
  • Move through the stages in order. Listed, sharing, receiving, joint planning; evidence at each one earns the next.
Gateway card

Before you commit to co-selling with a platform

  • One platform chosen, based on where most customers run
  • A one-page case for how your product grows the platform's consumption
  • Attribution set up with live customers
  • A written rule on what pipeline data is shared, approved by a named person
  • Co-sold win rate, cycle time and referred pipeline tracked quarterly

Common questions

What is co-selling with AWS?

Working joint customer opportunities with AWS sellers through the APN Customer Engagements (ACE) programme. Partners share and update opportunities in Partner Central and, once eligible, can receive referrals from AWS.

How do you get referrals from Microsoft or AWS sellers?

Show that your product increases customer consumption on the platform, meet the programme's tier or designation requirements, keep shared opportunities accurate, and set up partner attribution with your customers.

Is co-selling with cloud providers worth it for a small software company?

It can be if most customers run on one platform and the product adds workloads there. If customers are spread across clouds and the product consumes little, the return is usually weaker.

What is Partner Admin Link?

A Microsoft mechanism that links a partner's ID to its user or service principal in a customer's Azure environment, so Microsoft can attribute influenced and consumed revenue to that partner.

Sources and notes

  • AWS, APN Customer Engagements (ACE) Program and ACE overview. Vendor programme pages; incentive amounts are not published.
  • AWS, AWS Services Partner Tiers. Vendor programme page; requirements and benefits vary by geography and change.
  • Microsoft Learn, Partner capability score. Vendor documentation; per-metric weights not published on the page.
  • Microsoft Learn, Link a partner ID to your accounts (PAL and DPOR). Vendor documentation; Azure only.
  • AWS Marketplace, Channel Programs. Vendor page; source of the statement on spend commitments.
  • Microsoft Learn, Co-sell with Microsoft sales teams and partners overview, updated 5 October 2026. Vendor documentation; describes opportunity types but publishes no performance data.
  • Microsoft Learn, Co-sell requirements, updated 11 November 2026. Vendor documentation; source of co-sell-ready and Azure IP co-sell thresholds; requirements change often.
  • Google Cloud, Introducing Google Cloud Partner Network, 16 December 2025. Vendor announcement; describes tiers and competencies, not co-sell mechanics or incentive amounts.
  • Canalys, IT spending forecasts 2025. Analyst estimates; revised over time.
  • Ebsta, B2B Sales Benchmarks 2024. Vendor benchmark data; correlational.
  • Google Cloud's co-sell opportunity mechanics under the new Partner Network were not published in the sources reviewed. The four-stage model and measures are lowob's framework.

Next move

Write the one-page case for a platform account manager this week: the workload your product brings to the platform, the consumption a typical customer adds, and two customers who will vouch for it. If you cannot write it, co-selling is not yet your next move.
